Subject: Request: carveout for customer-managed WAN outages and evidence protocol

Hi Tessa,

Quick background: our production LLM endpoints are deployed in our VPC peered with Redwood's private deployment. Over the last quarter we've seen a handful of incidents where our transit provider had outages (BGP flaps / metro maintenance) that caused sustained latency to Redwood's edge. From Atlantic's standpoint these were clearly in our control, but our contracts with downstream teams require an exception to Redwood's uptime/latency commitments in those situations.

Can you propose language that:
- Excludes periods where Atlantic (or a third-party transit provider engaged by Atlantic) controls egress/ingress and the degradation is proven by network telemetry, and
- Defines the evidence we need to provide (logs, traceroutes, timestamps) so Redwood can attribute the incident to our network rather than its runtime?

We'll need this fairly quickly — legal wants an internal notification next week. Also include any operational requirements (log retention windows, formats) so our infra team can prepare.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Holt
Head of Cloud Ops, Atlantic BioTech

Samantha — thanks for the clear summary. We can support a narrowly scoped carveout for customer-managed transit outages, but we need a precise evidence and attribution process to avoid masking platform issues.

High-level proposal (I'll loop Legal and Infra):
- Carveout scope: periods where Atlantic or Atlantic's contracted transit provider is the proximate cause of reduced connectivity between Atlantic's VPC and Redwood's ingress points (we will require traceroutes, BGP logs, and observable packet loss/latency spikes).
- Evidence: time-stamped traceroutes from two points inside Atlantic's VPC, BGP withdraw/announce logs from your provider, and server-side ingress/drop metrics from your edge (90-day retention).
- Attribution window: Redwood will evaluate the provided evidence within 72 hours; if attribution is validated, time within the carveout is excluded from SLA calculations.
- Operational: provide daily aggregated exports (CSV) for flagged incidents during the 7-day review window and a one-click archive for legal review.

I'm attaching a first pass at SLA amendment language and an evidence template for your infra team to fill (20250313-sla-amendment-draft.docx). If this looks roughly right we'll bring in Karthik for technical wording and Neha for compliance/retention alignment.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Looping in a brief technical note on attribution and fallback behavior.

1) Attribution signals we can reliably use:
   - BGP withdraws/route changes at T that correlate with increased RTT/loss at Redwood's edge,
   - Consistent traceroute hops showing packet loss or different egress at the same time window from two independent VMs inside the customer's VPC,
   - TCP retransmits and SYN timeouts observed at the connection level to our ingress pool.

2) Evidence format: prefer machine-readable JSON export (time series slices) + human summary. Reducing manual interpretation accelerates our 72h check.

3) Fallback request: Atlantic asked about a guaranteed fallback to Redwood-hosted endpoints for critical traffic. We can offer a canary-hosted fallback option for a subset of endpoints with a warm standby, but that has cost and lead time implications (we estimate a recurring incremental reserve cost ~USD 8k/mo per critical endpoint and a 2-3 week prep/enrollment window).

4) SLO math: carveout will exclude validated time windows from uptime calculations; however, tail-latency SLOs that include cross-region routing may still be impacted and require separate exclusion language.

I'll propose redline text in the amendment (technical appendix) once Legal confirms retention boundaries.

— Karthik (Infra)
From: Mary Garcia <mary.garcia@atlanticbio.com>

Date: Sun, 16 Mar 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for customer-managed WAN outages and evidence protocol

Team — thanks for the quick turn. Our legal and networking teams reviewed the draft and provided redlines. High level requests: 

- Narrow the carveout to exclude only outages attributable to "customer-controlled transit providers" (explicitly call out backbone/transit ISP events) rather than any third-party service we use (so managed WAN appliances we operate remain covered unless the ISP is confirmed at fault).
- Evidence retention: Atlantic must retain the requested telemetry for 90 days and provide exports within 24 hours of an incident being flagged by either party. The retention requirement is to ensure auditors can validate claims.
- Fallback: Atlantic will take the canary-hosted fallback for two critical endpoints. We need the cost estimate (you mentioned ~8k/mo per endpoint) in writing and a short runbook describing failover triggers and expected RTO/RPO.

Attached are our redlined comments in-line on the doc (we converted your draft to comments) and a filled-in evidence example for a past incident (see: 20250312-evidence-template-wan.pdf).

Regards,
Mary Garcia
IT Operations, Atlantic BioTech

Mary, Samantha — thanks for the redlines and the sample evidence. Summary / next steps: 

- Agreement in principle: Redwood accepts a narrowly scoped carveout for "customer-controlled transit provider" incidents, with evidence-based attribution required. We will limit the carveout language to explicitly call out transit ISP/backbone events as requested.
- Retention & exports: Redwood requires the telemetry in the provided format; Atlantic will retain 90 days of telemetry and provide exports within 24 hours for flagged incidents. Operations will sign an access checklist to validate exports during a 7-day review window.
- Fallback & costs: Redwood will provision a warm standby hosted fallback for up to two critical endpoints at an initial recurring fee of USD 7,500/month per endpoint (we revised the estimate after infra sizing). We'll provide the RTO/RPO runbook and the enrollment checklist by EOD Friday.
- Legal & execution: copying Redwood Legal (legal@redwood.example.com). Please expect a DocuSign packet for the SLA amendment and a short operations checklist attached.

Attaching the finalized amendment PDF (20250318-sla-amendment-final.pdf) and the onboarding checklist for the hosted fallback. If that looks good I'll route to DocuSign and Ops will schedule a kickoff.
